quotes: LeakGuard runs under its own service account svc-leakguard.
The account is not used by any staff member and has no interactive login.
findings.model_reasoning: These sentences show LeakGuard uses a separate service account, distinct from staff logins. The account is explicitly not used by staff.

quotes: The svc-leakguard account may read sensor data and send alerts to the operations channel.
It has no permission to change pumps, valves or any plant setting.
findings.model_reasoning: The quoted lines limit the account to specific actions and explicitly deny broader plant-control permissions. They also state that permissions are reviewed quarterly.

quotes: Maria, operations lead, is responsible for LeakGuard.

findings.model_reasoning: The evidence names Maria as the responsible person and says she or the duty engineer can override or stop the agent's alerts. That matches the control.

quotes: A false alert has no effect on the network; staff check and dismiss it, and alert sending can be paused immediately.
findings.model_reasoning: This shows staff can take over manually and stop alert sending immediately. That indicates reversibility or rapid manual intervention.

quotes: Every LeakGuard action is written to the central log with time, account, action, target and result.

quotes: Logs are kept for 12 months and reviewed weekly by the duty engineer.
